title: Travel: John Lennon – Tokyo to London | 1971
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono left Japan for England on 20 January 1971.

They had set sail from Los Angeles on 30 December 1970, aboard the SS President Cleveland, arriving in Yokohama Port on 13 January. Just under two weeks later, they left Haneda Airport in Tokyo for London’s Heathrow Airport.

Earlier in the day, Lennon and Ono visited the Toshiba offices and met executives Kenji Mizuhara (Apple Records manager for Japan), T Ishizaka (general manager, Toshiba Musical Industries), and K Ueno (international A&R manager).

Lennon and Ono’s Japanese holiday was curtailed when his lawyers insisted he return to England to deal with the turmoil caused by Paul McCartney’s High Court action to dissolve The Beatles’ partnership.

The couple arrived back in the UK on 21 January, only to be told that they could have fulfilled their legal requirements by telephone. With some unexpected free time, the pair gave an interview to political writers and activists Tariq Ali and Robin Blackburn of the Marxist newspaper Red Mole. It was published in an edition dated 8–22 March 1971.
